full_target:
Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed.

parameters.type: integer submodule of the underlying integer module of V

hypotheses.statement: Let p be any prime, K any field of characteristic p, λ an integer with 0≤λ<p, V=V(λ) the complex irreducible highest-weight sl₂-module of dimension λ+1, and x,y,h its Chevalley operators satisfying hx−xh=2x, hy−yh=−2y, xy−yx=h. Let v∈V be nonzero with xv=0 and hv=λv. Let U_ℤ be the integer enveloping subalgebra generated by all X_r=x^r/r! and Y_r=y^r/r!, r≥0. Let M⊆V be any U_ℤ-stable free abelian subgroup with an integer basis also a complex basis of V. The target space is M⊗_ℤ K with the induced x,y,h actions and the Chevalley Lie algebra (ℤx+ℤy+ℤh)⊗_ℤ K, including characteristic two.
hypotheses.origin: problem.md:16–41; numbered-basis-graph.json H001 (complete original standing assumptions).

definitions.definition: ell=max(λ,0), regarded as a natural number (the integer-to-natural conversion λ.toNat). This definition imposes no range condition on λ.
J=Fin(ell+1), identified with the integers i satisfying 0≤i≤ell.

definitions.type: sequence of complex-linear endomorphisms of V
definitions.definition: For each natural r, X_r=(r! : ℂ)⁻¹ x^r, with x^0=Id_V. Factorials are the usual products, with 0!=1.

definitions.type: sequence of complex-linear endomorphisms of V
definitions.definition: For each natural r, Y_r=(r! : ℂ)⁻¹ y^r, with y^0=Id_V.
For i∈J set e_i=Y_i(v)=y^i(v)/i!; the index i denotes its natural value.

definitions.type: integer subalgebra of the universal enveloping algebra of sl₂(ℂ)
definitions.definition: U_ℤ is generated over ℤ by the divided powers x^r/r! and y^r/r! for all natural r. Its action on V is generated by the operators X_r,Y_r. Operator stability under this algebra means stability under every generator.

V_K=M⊗_ℤ K, with K acting on the second factor. This is the original V(K). For any f∈End_ℤ(M), f⊗Id_K acts by u⊗a↦f(u)⊗a. The original induced x,y,h actions are the tensor extensions of their restrictions to M; h|M=(x|M)(y|M)−(y|M)(x|M).
Q=K⊗_ℤ M, with K acting on the first factor.

definitions.type: sequence of integer-linear endomorphisms of M
definitions.definition: For every natural r, A_r=X_r|M, the restriction to M. Its construction requires the original admissibility hypothesis that every X_r preserves M. In particular A_1=x|M and A_0=Id_M.

definitions.type: sequence of integer-linear endomorphisms of M
definitions.definition: For every natural r, B_r=Y_r|M, the restriction to M. Its construction requires the original admissibility hypothesis that every Y_r preserves M. In particular B_1=y|M and B_0=Id_M.
For i,j∈J let s_ij=j!(ell−j)! A_(ell−i) B_ell A_ell B_(ell−j), with integer scalar multiplication. Products of endomorphisms mean composition with the right factor first.
d=(ell!:K), the image of the natural factorial under ℤ→K. No nonvanishing is assumed by this definition.

For f∈End_ℤ(M), Fext(f)=Id_K⊗f is the scalar extension obtained by the balanced tensor construction; on pure tensors Fext(f)(a⊗u)=a⊗f(u). Its additivity, multiplicativity, unitality and compatibility with integer scalars are conclusions to prove when used.
For i,j∈J define U_ij=d⁻¹ Fext(s_ij). Here inverse is the total field operation, with 0⁻¹=0; no matrix-unit identity or invertibility is granted by this definition.

τ is the balanced tensor map specified by τ(u⊗a)=a⊗u. The scalar action on V_K is on its second factor and on Q on its first factor. Bijectivity and operator intertwining are assertions to prove, rather than part of this definition.
